title: François Couperin
k: francois couperin 1668–1733 · the baroque a parisian organist whose harpsichord pieces turn ornament, delayed resolution and the timing of a released key into structural events.

title: Messe pour les paroisses · Messe pour les couvents
k: messe pour les paroisses · messe pour les couvents francois couperin ·  · 1690 organ, alternating with sung liturgy two sequences of liturgical organ pieces. registrations and the position of the solo line determine the sound as directly as the notes.

title: Premier Livre de pièces de clavecin
k: premier livre de pieces de clavecin francois couperin ·  · 1713 harpsichord ordres 1–5. conventional dances coexist with named pieces; couperin supplies a detailed table of ornaments.

title: Leçons de Ténèbres pour le Mercredy
k: lecons de tenebres pour le mercredy francois couperin ·  · 1714 one or two high voices and continuo three surviving lessons on the lamentations of jeremiah. elaborate hebrew-letter melismas frame more direct declamation of the latin verses.

title: L’Art de toucher le clavecin
k: l’art de toucher le clavecin francois couperin ·  · 1716–17 harpsichord; pedagogical treatise with pieces fingering, touch and ornament explained through practical instructions, an allemande and eight preludes.

title: Second Livre de pièces de clavecin
k: second livre de pieces de clavecin francois couperin ·  · 1717 harpsichord; two instruments in selected pieces ordres 6–12, including les barricades mysterieuses and the two-harpsichord allemande a deux clavecins.

title: Troisième Livre de pièces de clavecin · Concerts royaux
k: troisieme livre de pieces de clavecin · concerts royaux francois couperin ·  · 1722 harpsichord; flexible chamber ensemble for the concerts ordres 13–19 and four chamber concerts. the thirteenth ordre includes the sequence of masked characters les folies francoises, ou les dominos.

title: Les Goûts-réunis · L’Apothéose de Corelli · L’Apothéose de Lully
k: les gouts-reunis · l’apotheose de corelli · l’apotheose de lully francois couperin ·  · 1724–25 chamber ensemble with continuo french and italian practices are joined through dance, sonata and explicitly programmatic tributes to the two composers.

title: Les Nations
k: les nations francois couperin ·  · 1726 two treble instruments and continuo four large ordres, each coupling an italianate sonata with french dances: la francoise, l’espagnole, l’imperiale and la piemontoise.

title: Pièces de violes
k: pieces de violes francois couperin ·  · 1728 bass viol and continuo two suites; the second ends with la pompe funebre and la chemise-blanche. bowed sustain gives the suspensions a different physical presence from the keyboard pieces.

title: Quatrième Livre de pièces de clavecin
k: quatrieme livre de pieces de clavecin francois couperin ·  · 1730 harpsichord ordres 20–27. the final book continues the mixture of social portrait, dance and instrumental character piece.

title: Antonio Vivaldi
k: antonio vivaldi 1678–1741 · the baroque a violinist and theatre composer who made the returning orchestral refrain organise a soloist’s changing keys, textures and physical risks.

title: L’estro armonico
k: l’estro armonico antonio vivaldi · op. 3 · 1711 twelve concertos for one, two or four violins, with strings and continuo the amsterdam publication that spread vivaldi’s concerto procedures across europe. six concertos became the basis of bach transcriptions.

title: Stabat Mater
k: stabat mater antonio vivaldi · rv 621 · 1712 alto solo, strings and continuo a compact f minor setting of the opening portion of the sequence. music from the first movements returns later in the text, making repetition part of the lament.

title: Ottone in villa
k: ottone in villa antonio vivaldi · rv 729 · 1713 opera in three acts first performed in vicenza. the relatively small cast and orchestral forces expose the mechanics of the da capo aria.

title: Gloria in D major
k: gloria in d major antonio vivaldi · rv 589 · c. 1715 soloists, chorus, trumpet, oboe, strings and continuo twelve movements distribute the text between public choral declaration and more intimate solo writing. the opening d major is interrupted by the b minor et in terra pax.

title: Juditha triumphans
k: juditha triumphans antonio vivaldi · rv 644 · 1716 five vocal soloists, female chorus and varied instrumental ensemble a latin oratorio for the pieta, connecting the biblical judith with venice’s wartime circumstances. its instrumentation extends well beyond the normal string-and-continuo group.

title: The Four Seasons
k: the four seasons antonio vivaldi · op. 8 nos. 1–4; rv 269, 315, 293, 297 · 1725 solo violin, strings and continuo spring in e major, summer in g minor, autumn in f major and winter in f minor. printed sonnets and lettered references make the programme unusually explicit.

title: Orlando furioso
k: orlando furioso antonio vivaldi · rv 728 · 1727 opera in three acts ariosto’s characters become vehicles for jealousy, deception and madness. sol da te, mio dolce amore joins the voice to an extended obbligato flute part.

title: Six Flute Concertos
k: six flute concertos antonio vivaldi · op. 10 · c. 1728–29 flute, strings and continuo includes la tempesta di mare, la notte and il gardellino. several works rework earlier versions for different instrumental combinations.

title: Griselda
k: griselda antonio vivaldi · rv 718 · 1735 opera in three acts carlo goldoni adapted an earlier libretto by apostolo zeno. agitata da due venti translates the image of competing winds into breath-testing vocal passagework.

title: Jean-Philippe Rameau
k: jean-philippe rameau 1683–1764 · the baroque a theorist of chord roots who began his operatic career at fifty and made harmonic surprise part of french theatrical action.

title: Premier Livre de pièces de clavecin
k: premier livre de pieces de clavecin jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1706 harpsichord a suite beginning with a prelude that retains an unmeasured opening. the french dance tradition supplies the collection’s framework.

title: Pièces de clavecin
k: pieces de clavecin jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1724 harpsichord includes le rappel des oiseaux, les tendres plaintes, les cyclopes and the e minor suite. rameau also explains aspects of keyboard technique.

title: Nouvelles Suites de pièces de clavecin
k: nouvelles suites de pieces de clavecin jean-philippe rameau ·  · c. 1728 harpsichord includes la poule, les sauvages, l’enharmonique and the gavotte with six doubles: a repeated harmonic design becomes a succession of technical problems.

title: Hippolyte et Aricie
k: hippolyte et aricie jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1733 tragedie en musique, soloists, chorus and orchestra rameau’s first opera, with a libretto by pellegrin after racine and classical sources. the underworld scene makes harmonic instability part of the drama.

title: Les Indes galantes
k: les indes galantes jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1735–36 opera-ballet, soloists, chorus, dancers and orchestra a prologue and separate entrees in imagined non-european settings. the north american entree, les sauvages, was added in 1736.

title: Castor et Pollux
k: castor et pollux jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1737; revised 1754 tragedie en musique brotherly devotion and romantic rivalry lead from mourning to the underworld and apotheosis. the two principal versions differ substantially in dramatic construction.

title: Dardanus
k: dardanus jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1739; revised 1744 tragedie en musique an opera repeatedly reworked after objections to its libretto. hear its instrumental and vocal scenes within the chosen version.

title: Pièces de clavecin en concerts
k: pieces de clavecin en concerts jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1741 harpsichord with violin or flute and bass viol or second violin five concerts led by a written-out keyboard part. several movements carry the names of people in rameau’s circle.

title: Platée
k: platee jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1745 comic stage work with high-tenor title role, chorus and orchestra a divine deception staged for a marsh nymph. la folie’s scene makes virtuoso singing itself part of the comedy.

title: Les Boréades
k: les boreades jean-philippe rameau ·  · 1763 tragedie en musique in five acts rehearsed but not publicly staged during rameau’s lifetime. dynastic restrictions and a storm generated by boreas give the orchestra a central dramatic role.

title: Johann Sebastian Bach
k: johann sebastian bach 1685–1750 · the baroque an organist, teacher and church musician who made a bass line, a dance rhythm and a fugue subject carry the same argument.

title: Aus der Tiefen rufe ich, Herr, zu dir
k: aus der tiefen rufe ich, herr, zu dir johann sebastian bach · bwv 131 · 1707–08 soloists, chorus, oboe, strings and continuo an early sacred concerto on psalm 130. chorale lines sound above the individual supplication.

title: Orgelbüchlein
k: orgelbuchlein johann sebastian bach · bwv 599–644 · c. 1708–17 organ forty-six completed chorale preludes in a projected collection with many more titles. a concise school of obbligato pedal playing and motivic accompaniment.

title: Weinen, Klagen, Sorgen, Zagen
k: weinen, klagen, sorgen, zagen johann sebastian bach · bwv 12 · 1714 soloists, chorus, trumpet, oboe, strings and continuo the opening chorus uses a descending chromatic bass; bach later adapted its central material for the crucifixus of the b minor mass.

title: Six Cello Suites
k: six cello suites johann sebastian bach · bwv 1007–1012 · c. 1717–23 unaccompanied cello; five-string instrument specified for no. 6 preludes followed by dances. the fifth asks for the top string to be retuned; the sixth extends the register beyond the normal four-string cello.

title: Sonatas and Partitas for Solo Violin
k: sonatas and partitas for solo violin johann sebastian bach · bwv 1001–1006 · 1720 unaccompanied violin three four-movement sonatas alternate with three dance collections. the d minor partita ends with the chaconne, a sustained variation structure built from a recurring harmonic scheme.

title: Six Brandenburg Concertos
k: six brandenburg concertos johann sebastian bach · bwv 1046–1051 · 1721 six different instrumental ensembles the dedication is dated 1721; the music draws on earlier work. each concerto proposes a different relationship between solo group, ensemble and bass.

title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I
k: the well-tempered clavier, book i johann sebastian bach · bwv 846–869 · 1722 keyboard twenty-four preludes and fugues, moving chromatically from c major and c minor to b major and b minor. the title leaves the choice of temperament open.

title: Inventions and Sinfonias
k: inventions and sinfonias johann sebastian bach · bwv 772–801 · 1723 keyboard fifteen two-part and fifteen three-part pieces. bach’s title page connects clear voice-leading with a singing style of execution and the acquisition of compositional ideas.

title: St John Passion
k: st john passion johann sebastian bach · bwv 245 · 1724 soloists, chorus, orchestra and continuo the evangelist’s narration is interrupted by arias, chorales and tightly organised crowd choruses. bach revised the work repeatedly after its first leipzig performance.

title: St Matthew Passion
k: st matthew passion johann sebastian bach · bwv 244 · 1727; revised 1736 soloists, two choirs and orchestras, additional soprano ripieno a double-ensemble design with poetry by picander. the opening chorus places a chorale above an exchange between the two principal choirs.

title: Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme
k: wachet auf, ruft uns die stimme johann sebastian bach · bwv 140 · 1731 soloists, chorus, horn, oboes, taille, strings and continuo philipp nicolai’s hymn supplies three structural pillars. between them, the dialogue of soul and christ becomes chamber music for soprano, bass and obbligato instrument.

title: Christmas Oratorio
k: christmas oratorio johann sebastian bach · bwv 248 · 1734–35 soloists, chorus and orchestra six cantatas for six services from christmas day to epiphany. much of the music adapts earlier secular cantatas.

title: Italian Concerto
k: italian concerto johann sebastian bach · bwv 971 · 1735 two-manual harpsichord a concerto without orchestra. marked contrasts of forte and piano distinguish ensemble-like statements from solo passages; the slow movement sets an embellished line over a steady accompaniment.

title: Clavier-Übung III
k: clavier-ubung iii johann sebastian bach ·  · 1739 organ the e♭ major prelude and fugue bwv 552 frame chorale settings and four duets. large settings with pedal stand beside smaller manualiter versions.

title: The Art of Fugue
sub: Johann Sebastian Bach · BWV 1080 · c. 1740–50; published 1751
k: the art of fugue johann sebastian bach · bwv 1080 · c. 1740–50; published 1751 unspecified; normally performed on keyboard or by instrumental ensemble a d minor subject is developed through fugues and canons, including mirror counterpoint. the surviving final, unfinished fugue introduces the notes b♭–a–c–b♮.

title: Goldberg Variations
k: goldberg variations johann sebastian bach · bwv 988 · 1741 two-manual harpsichord aria, thirty variations and the returning aria. canons at successively larger intervals alternate with character pieces and passages designed around two-manual technique.

title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book II
k: the well-tempered clavier, book ii johann sebastian bach · bwv 870–893 · c. 1742 keyboard a second traversal of all twenty-four keys, assembled from music of different dates. the preludes range from compact inventions to extended binary movements.

title: The Musical Offering
k: the musical offering johann sebastian bach · bwv 1079 · 1747 keyboard and chamber instruments; trio sonata for flute, violin and continuo ricercars, puzzle canons and a trio sonata on the theme supplied by frederick ii. the six-part ricercar treats its chromatic subject in a particularly dense texture.

title: Mass in B minor
k: mass in b minor johann sebastian bach · bwv 232 · 1748–49, assembled soloists, chorus, orchestra and continuo a complete latin ordinary assembled from several decades of work. the crucifixus reuses the lament bass of bwv 12; the following et resurrexit changes metre, register and instrumental weight.

title: George Frideric Handel
k: george frideric handel 1685–1759 · the baroque a german-trained composer of italian opera who made the english chorus an actor in public musical drama.

title: Dixit Dominus
k: dixit dominus george frideric handel · hwv 232 · 1707 soloists, five-part chorus, strings and continuo a latin psalm setting from the roman years. the vocal writing demands both rapid articulation and the ability to sustain dissonant notes against moving parts.

title: Agrippina
k: agrippina george frideric handel · hwv 6 · 1709 opera in three acts a venetian political comedy whose characters manipulate one another through changing claims and disguises. handel adapts substantial amounts of earlier music.

title: Rinaldo
k: rinaldo george frideric handel · hwv 7 · 1711 opera in three acts handel’s first london opera, drawing on tasso’s crusading epic. the spectacle and virtuoso arias include music reworked from earlier italian compositions.

title: Water Music
k: water music george frideric handel · hwv 348–350 · 1717 orchestra with horns, trumpets and woodwinds associated with george i’s thames excursion of july 1717. the surviving suites combine french overture writing, dances and concerto-like exchanges.

title: Giulio Cesare in Egitto
k: giulio cesare in egitto george frideric handel · hwv 17 · 1724 opera in three acts political and erotic manoeuvres generate sharply differentiated arias. in va tacito e nascosto, a horn participates in caesar’s image of the stealthy hunter.

title: Alexander’s Feast
k: alexander’s feast george frideric handel · hwv 75 · 1736 soloists, chorus and orchestra dryden’s ode becomes a demonstration of music’s power over alexander. the changing emotions are carried by a sequence of instrumental, solo and choral characters.

title: Twelve Concerti grossi
k: twelve concerti grossi george frideric handel · op. 6; hwv 319–330 · 1739 concertino of two violins and cello, string orchestra and continuo corelli’s model is expanded through overtures, dances, fugues and contrasting solo episodes.

title: Messiah
sub: George Frideric Handel · HWV 56 · 1741; first performed 1742
k: messiah george frideric handel · hwv 56 · 1741; first performed 1742 soloists, chorus, orchestra and continuo jennens’s scriptural compilation moves from prophecy through passion to resurrection. handel’s revisions for successive casts make the choice of version a real performance decision.

title: Music for the Royal Fireworks
k: music for the royal fireworks george frideric handel · hwv 351 · 1749 large wind band with percussion; later version includes strings written for the celebration of the treaty of aix-la-chapelle. handel adapted the initial outdoor forces for later concert performance.

title: Jephtha
sub: George Frideric Handel · HWV 70 · 1751; first performed 1752
k: jephtha george frideric handel · hwv 70 · 1751; first performed 1752 soloists, chorus and orchestra handel’s final oratorio, interrupted during composition by failing sight. the father’s vow and its consequences give the soloists and chorus conflicting ethical positions.

title: Domenico Scarlatti
k: domenico scarlatti 1685–1757 · the baroque an italian court musician in lisbon and madrid who made keyboard sonatas out of hand crossings, repeated notes and abrupt changes of harmonic ground.

title: Stabat Mater
k: stabat mater domenico scarlatti ·  · probably c. 1715 ten voices and continuo usually associated with the roman period, though its precise date and original occasion are uncertain. four soprano parts and pairs of lower voices form changing contrapuntal combinations.

title: Essercizi per gravicembalo
k: essercizi per gravicembalo domenico scarlatti · k. 1–30 · 1738–39, publication keyboard thirty pieces dedicated to joao v of portugal. the d minor k. 9 uses a pastoral compound metre; the g minor k. 30 ends the collection with a fugue.

title: Sonata in B minor
k: sonata in b minor domenico scarlatti · k. 87 · 1742, venice copy keyboard a slow, closely worked contrapuntal texture. the date belongs to the manuscript volume.

title: Sonata in D major
k: sonata in d major domenico scarlatti · k. 119 · 1749, venice copy keyboard repeated chords, crowded dissonances and abrupt changes of texture make the keyboard’s attack part of the formal argument.

title: Sonata in A major
k: sonata in a major domenico scarlatti · k. 208 · 1753, venice copy keyboard marked adagio e cantabile. a decorated upper line asks for continuity without turning the accompaniment into a blurred sustained chord.

title: Sonata in E major
k: sonata in e major domenico scarlatti · k. 380 · 1754, venice copy keyboard a ceremonial, rhythmically pointed piece in triple metre. its repeated gestures need differentiated articulation.

title: Sonata in F minor
k: sonata in f minor domenico scarlatti · k. 466 · 1756, venice copy keyboard a slow sonata whose moving inner texture and suspensions demand control of separate durations. the date records the manuscript copy.

title: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach
k: carl philipp emanuel bach 1714–1788 · classical a keyboard player who made hesitation, interruption and a change of mind into musical form.

title: Six Prussian Sonatas
k: six prussian sonatas carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 48 · 1742 keyboard published with a dedication to frederick ii. three-movement designs whose slow movements make ornamentation and changing affect central to the argument.

title: Six Württemberg Sonatas
k: six wurttemberg sonatas carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 49 · 1744 keyboard the set extends the range of keys and rhetorical contrasts of the prussian collection.

title: Cello Concerto in A minor
k: cello concerto in a minor carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 170 · 1750 solo cello, strings and continuo angular orchestral gestures surround a solo part that alternates athletic passagework and sustained melodic declamation.

title: Fantasia in C minor
sub: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach · Wq 63/6, third movement · 1753
k: fantasia in c minor carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 63/6, third movement · 1753 keyboard the final movement of the sixth probestuck accompanying the first part of the versuch. a practical demonstration of changing affect and free delivery.

title: Geistliche Oden und Lieder
k: geistliche oden und lieder carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 194 · 1758 voice and keyboard; poems by c. f. gellert fifty-four devotional songs, designed for domestic use as well as attentive musical study. the keyboard takes an expressive role alongside the voice.

title: Six String Symphonies
k: six string symphonies carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 182 · 1773 strings and continuo written for baron van swieten. unison attacks, wide intervals and unexpected junctions between movements make small forces sound volatile.

title: Die Auferstehung und Himmelfahrt Jesu
sub: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach · Wq 240 · 1774; revised 1778
k: die auferstehung und himmelfahrt jesu carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 240 · 1774; revised 1778 soloists, chorus and orchestra ramler’s resurrection and ascension oratorio, with reflective arias, narrative recitatives and large public choruses.

title: Four Orchestral Symphonies
k: four orchestral symphonies carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 183 · 1775–76 orchestra with independent wind parts published as symphonies with twelve obbligato parts. the d major opening makes a repeated note and dislocated accents into a large-scale provocation.

title: Heilig
k: heilig carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 217 · 1776 alto, two choirs and orchestral groups an introductory arietta leads to an antiphonal setting of the sanctus in german. the contrast between angelic and human choirs is architectural as well as harmonic.

title: Fantasia in F♯ minor
k: fantasia in f♯ minor carl philipp emanuel bach · wq 67 · 1787 keyboard a late free fantasia whose passages of measured motion alternate with recitative-like writing. a related version with violin bears the title c. p. e. bachs empfindungen.

title: Joseph Haydn
k: joseph haydn 1732–1809 · classical a court musician who taught the symphony and quartet to argue with the listener’s expectations.

title: Symphony No. 6 in D major “Le Matin”
k: symphony no. 6 in d major “le matin” joseph haydn · hob. i:6 · 1761 orchestra a slow sunrise introduction leads to concertante writing for individual players, including an unusually prominent double bass in the trio.

title: Symphony No. 45 in F♯ minor “Farewell”
k: symphony no. 45 in f♯ minor “farewell” joseph haydn · hob. i:45 · 1772 orchestra an agitated minor-key symphony whose finale changes tempo and sheds players one by one. the last two violinists finish in f♯ major.

title: Six String Quartets, Op. 20
k: six string quartets, op. 20 joseph haydn · hob. iii:31–36 · 1772 two violins, viola and cello cello-led themes, independent inner parts and three fugal finales. the later nickname “sun” comes from a publisher’s decoration.

title: Six String Quartets, Op. 33
k: six string quartets, op. 33 joseph haydn · hob. iii:37–42 · 1781 string quartet the set containing the “joke” and “bird” quartets. conversational exchanges and rhythmic misdirection keep all four players active.

title: Six Paris Symphonies, Nos. 82–87
k: six paris symphonies, nos. 82–87 joseph haydn · hob. i:82–87 · 1785–86 orchestra written for the concert de la loge olympique. no. 83 in g minor sets a sharply articulated opening against the repeated-note accompaniment that earned its “hen” nickname.

title: The Seven Last Words of Our Saviour on the Cross
k: the seven last words of our saviour on the cross joseph haydn · hob. xx:1 · 1786 originally orchestra; later versions include string quartet and oratorio an introduction, seven slow meditations and an earthquake. commissioned for devotional use in cadiz; the problem is how to sustain contrast across a sequence of slow movements.

title: Symphony No. 94 in G major “Surprise”
k: symphony no. 94 in g major “surprise” joseph haydn · hob. i:94 · 1791–92 orchestra the loud chord interrupts a quiet c major variation theme. the subsequent variations carry the movement’s argument forward.

title: Variations in F minor
k: variations in f minor joseph haydn · hob. xvii:6 · 1793 keyboard a double-variation design alternating minor and major. its expanded minor-key coda unsettles the apparent symmetry of the preceding sequence.

title: Symphony No. 104 in D major “London”
k: symphony no. 104 in d major “london” joseph haydn · hob. i:104 · 1795 orchestra the last numbered symphony. a severe d minor introduction precedes the major-key allegro; the finale places its tune over a drone-like bass.

title: Trumpet Concerto in E♭ major
k: trumpet concerto in e♭ major joseph haydn · hob. viie:1 · 1796 keyed trumpet and orchestra written for anton weidinger. the soloist’s chromatic notes in the middle register advertise an instrument freed from the natural trumpet’s harmonic-series limits.

title: Missa in tempore belli
k: missa in tempore belli joseph haydn · hob. xxii:9 · 1796 soloists, chorus and orchestra the “mass in time of war”. timpani disturb the agnus dei’s appeal for peace; military signs enter the liturgical structure.

title: String Quartet in C major “Emperor”
sub: Joseph Haydn · Op. 76 No. 3; Hob. III:77 · 1797
k: string quartet in c major “emperor” joseph haydn · op. 76 no. 3; hob. iii:77 · 1797 string quartet the slow movement varies haydn’s new imperial hymn. the tune passes between players while counter-lines, register and texture change around it.

title: Die Schöpfung
k: die schopfung joseph haydn · hob. xxi:2 · 1796–98 soloists, chorus and orchestra creation narrated by three archangels, followed by adam and eve. chaos, light, birds, beasts and the human voice receive distinct musical treatments.

title: Die Jahreszeiten
k: die jahreszeiten joseph haydn · hob. xxi:3 · 1799–1801 three soloists, chorus and orchestra van swieten adapts james thomson. work songs, a summer storm, hunting horns and winter’s moral reflections fill four seasonal sections.

title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
k: wolfgang amadeus mozart 1756–1791 · classical an opera composer whose instrumental music gives different voices the freedom to disagree.

title: Symphony No. 25 in G minor
k: symphony no. 25 in g minor wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 183 · 1773 orchestra with four horns syncopations, unison attacks and wide leaps drive the first movement. four horns broaden the harmonic resources and weight of the wind group.

title: Violin Concerto No. 5 in A major
k: violin concerto no. 5 in a major wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 219 · 1775 solo violin and orchestra the soloist first enters at a slower tempo than the orchestral opening. the finale interrupts its minuet with a noisy minor-key episode conventionally labelled “turkish”.

title: Piano Concerto No. 9 in E♭ major “Jenamy”
k: piano concerto no. 9 in e♭ major “jenamy” wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 271 · 1777 piano and orchestra an early solo interruption changes the orchestra–piano relationship. the c minor slow movement carries the declamatory weight of an operatic scena.

title: Idomeneo, re di Creta
k: idomeneo, re di creta wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 366 · 1781 opera seria in three acts a father’s vow endangers his son. choruses, orchestral recitative and the sea-monster episode stretch the conventional sequence of solo arias.

title: Die Entführung aus dem Serail
k: die entfuhrung aus dem serail wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 384 · 1782 german singspiel in three acts konstanze’s demanding arias coexist with spoken dialogue, comic bass writing for osmin and “turkish” percussion in the orchestra.

title: Six Quartets dedicated to Haydn
k: six quartets dedicated to haydn wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 387, 421, 428, 458, 464, 465 · 1782–85 string quartet from contrapuntal finales to the suspended tonality of the “dissonance” introduction. the dedication acknowledges a living colleague.

title: Piano Concerto No. 20 in D minor
k: piano concerto no. 20 in d minor wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 466 · 1785 piano and orchestra syncopated strings destabilise the opening before the piano enters with its own material. beethoven later supplied cadenzas for the first and last movements.

title: Piano Concerto No. 23 in A major
k: piano concerto no. 23 in a major wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 488 · 1786 piano and orchestra with clarinets a major frames an adagio in f♯ minor. wind exchanges are integral to the first movement’s development.

title: Le nozze di Figaro
k: le nozze di figaro wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 492 · 1786 opera buffa in four acts; libretto by da ponte one day in a household where a planned wedding threatens the count’s authority. the act ii finale builds from a domestic dispute into a full ensemble through successive entrances.

title: String Quintets in C major and G minor
k: string quintets in c major and g minor wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 515 and 516 · 1787 two violins, two violas and cello the added viola expands the centre of the texture. k. 516’s muted adagio and slow introduction to the finale resist an uncomplicated move from g minor to major.

title: Don Giovanni
k: don giovanni wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 527 · 1787 dramma giocoso in two acts; libretto by da ponte comedy, attempted seduction and supernatural punishment. prague and vienna versions differ; the final ensemble after giovanni’s destruction restores the surviving characters’ separate viewpoints.

title: Symphonies Nos. 39, 40 and 41
k: symphonies nos. 39, 40 and 41 wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 543, 550, 551 · 1788 orchestra e♭ major, g minor and c major. the “jupiter” finale makes contrapuntal combination part of a sonata design; no. 40 survives with and without clarinets.

title: Così fan tutte
k: cosi fan tutte wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 588 · 1790 opera buffa in two acts; libretto by da ponte a wager about fidelity produces a formally symmetrical experiment whose music repeatedly complicates the experimenters’ assumptions.

title: La clemenza di Tito
k: la clemenza di tito wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 621 · 1791 opera seria in two acts written for the prague coronation. obligato clarinet and basset horn give two major arias unusually individual instrumental partners.

title: Die Zauberflöte
k: die zauberflote wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 620 · 1791 german singspiel in two acts; libretto by schikaneder popular theatre and initiation drama share a stage. the queen’s high coloratura, sarastro’s low bass and papageno’s song define different modes of authority and desire.

title: Clarinet Concerto in A major
k: clarinet concerto in a major wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 622 · 1791 basset clarinet and orchestra written for anton stadler’s instrument with notes below the ordinary clarinet’s range. modern basset-clarinet performances restore the low-register shape of the solo line.

title: Requiem in D minor
k: requiem in d minor wolfgang amadeus mozart · k. 626 · 1791 soloists, chorus, orchestra and organ unfinished. the standard completion is by sussmayr; modern editions offer alternatives. basset horns and bassoons give the surviving opening a dark wind sonority.

title: Ludwig van Beethoven
k: ludwig van beethoven 1770–1827 · classical a pianist who turned small rhythmic cells into long arguments, then rebuilt the forms that contained them.

title: Three Piano Trios
k: three piano trios ludwig van beethoven · op. 1 · 1793–95 piano, violin and cello four-movement designs give the ensemble unusual breadth. the third trio’s c minor is a tonal and rhetorical alternative to the first two major-key works.

title: Piano Sonata No. 8 in C minor “Pathétique”
k: piano sonata no. 8 in c minor “pathetique” ludwig van beethoven · op. 13 · 1798–99 piano the grave introduction returns within the first movement. slow declamation and the driving allegro remain separate forces throughout.

title: Piano Sonata No. 14 in C♯ minor
k: piano sonata no. 14 in c♯ minor ludwig van beethoven · op. 27 no. 2 · 1801 piano marked sonata quasi una fantasia. the posthumous “moonlight” nickname obscures a cycle that places its fastest and most disruptive movement last.

title: Symphony No. 3 in E♭ major “Eroica”
k: symphony no. 3 in e♭ major “eroica” ludwig van beethoven · op. 55 · 1802–04 orchestra with three horns an extended first movement, funeral march, scherzo and variation finale. the opening cello theme’s c♯ unsettles e♭ major within its first phrase.

title: Piano Sonata No. 21 in C major “Waldstein”
k: piano sonata no. 21 in c major “waldstein” ludwig van beethoven · op. 53 · 1803–04 piano the exposition turns towards e major. a short slow introduction links to the rondo, whose sustained pedal and wide registers depend on a changing conception of piano sound.

title: Piano Concerto No. 4 in G major
k: piano concerto no. 4 in g major ludwig van beethoven · op. 58 · 1804–06 piano and orchestra the piano begins alone; the orchestra answers in b major. the slow movement opposes terse string unisons to the soloist’s quiet, chordal replies.

title: Three “Razumovsky” Quartets
k: three “razumovsky” quartets ludwig van beethoven · op. 59 · 1806 string quartet large designs written for count andrey razumovsky. russian themes occur in nos. 1 and 2; no. 3 ends with a fast, fugal finale.

title: Violin Concerto in D major
k: violin concerto in d major ludwig van beethoven · op. 61 · 1806 violin and orchestra repeated timpani notes begin the first movement. the soloist’s high register and elaboration develop against an orchestral structure of unusual breadth.

title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor
k: symphony no. 5 in c minor ludwig van beethoven · op. 67 · 1804–08 orchestra, enlarged in the finale the four-note opening becomes a resource across the cycle. a transition over timpani and strings links the scherzo to a c major finale with new instruments.

title: Symphony No. 6 in F major “Pastoral”
k: symphony no. 6 in f major “pastoral” ludwig van beethoven · op. 68 · 1807–08 orchestra five movements with descriptive headings. repetition, drones and slowly changing harmony create a different sense of duration from the fifth.

title: Piano Concerto No. 5 in E♭ major
k: piano concerto no. 5 in e♭ major ludwig van beethoven · op. 73 · 1809 piano and orchestra orchestral chords alternate with written-out solo flourishes at the start. the “emperor” nickname was not beethoven’s; the slow movement leads directly into the finale.

title: Symphony No. 7 in A major
k: symphony no. 7 in a major ludwig van beethoven · op. 92 · 1811–12 orchestra each movement establishes a persistent rhythmic character. the a minor allegretto builds a processional pattern through successive layers and contrapuntal entries.

title: Fidelio
k: fidelio ludwig van beethoven · op. 72 · 1805–14 opera in two acts in its final version leonore rescues florestan from political imprisonment. three principal versions and four overtures document beethoven’s continuing revision of the theatrical problem.

title: Piano Sonata No. 29 in B♭ major “Hammerklavier”
k: piano sonata no. 29 in b♭ major “hammerklavier” ludwig van beethoven · op. 106 · 1817–18 piano a large four-movement sonata with an f♯ minor adagio and an extended final fugue. leaps and trills become contrapuntal material.

title: Piano Sonata No. 32 in C minor
k: piano sonata no. 32 in c minor ludwig van beethoven · op. 111 · 1821–22 piano two movements only. the c major arietta transforms a simple theme through changes of subdivision, register and sustained resonance.

title: Missa solemnis in D major
k: missa solemnis in d major ludwig van beethoven · op. 123 · 1819–23 four soloists, chorus, orchestra and organ a liturgical text on a concert scale. a solo violin descends into the benedictus; martial sounds interrupt the agnus dei’s prayer for peace.

title: Thirty-three Variations on a Waltz by Diabelli
k: thirty-three variations on a waltz by diabelli ludwig van beethoven · op. 120 · 1819–23 piano the theme is taken apart into repeated chords, turns, bass patterns and cadences. fugue and a final minuet transform its proportions.

title: Symphony No. 9 in D minor
k: symphony no. 9 in d minor ludwig van beethoven · op. 125 · 1822–24 four soloists, chorus and orchestra the finale reviews earlier movements, introduces the joy theme instrumentally and then turns to schiller’s words. the opening’s bare fifth withholds a clear major or minor identity.

title: The Late Quartets
k: the late quartets ludwig van beethoven · opp. 127, 130–133, 135 · 1824–26 string quartet five quartets and the separately published grosse fuge. the seven movements of op. 131 and the modal thanksgiving of op. 132 test different ways of organising an entire cycle.

title: Franz Schubert
k: franz schubert 1797–1828 · romanticism a viennese songwriter who made the piano an equal narrator, and carried the harmonic dislocations of the lied into symphonies and chamber music.

title: Gretchen am Spinnrade · Erlkönig
k: gretchen am spinnrade · erlkonig franz schubert · d. 118 · d. 328 · 1814–15 voice and piano; poems by goethe two early goethe settings. in gretchen (d minor, 1814), the spinning-wheel accompaniment stops at the kiss; in erlkonig (g minor, 1815), one singer distinguishes narrator, father, child and supernatural tempter while the pianist maintains repeated triplets.

title: Piano Quintet in A major “Trout”
k: piano quintet in a major “trout” franz schubert · d. 667 · 1819 piano, violin, viola, cello and double bass written for the circle of sylvester paumgartner in steyr. five movements, with a fourth-movement variation set on the song die forelle. the double bass separates the bass function from the cello; the song’s rippling accompaniment is withheld until the last variation.

title: Symphony in B minor “Unfinished”
k: symphony in b minor “unfinished” franz schubert · d. 759 · 1822 orchestra two completed movements, allegro moderato and andante con moto, followed in the manuscript by an incomplete scherzo. low strings begin alone; oboe and clarinet then sing over a string tremolo. johann herbeck conducted the first performance in vienna in december 1865.

title: Wanderer Fantasy in C major
k: wanderer fantasy in c major franz schubert · d. 760 · 1822 piano four linked sections share the long–short–short rhythm of der wanderer, d. 489. the c♯ minor adagio quotes the song; the final section turns its material into a fugue. liszt later arranged the work for piano and orchestra.

title: Die schöne Müllerin
k: die schone mullerin franz schubert · d. 795 · 1823 voice and piano; twenty poems by wilhelm muller a young miller follows a brook to employment, love and rejection. strophic songs keep the language of work and folk song audible; altered accompaniments and shifts of mode undermine the protagonist’s confidence. the brook takes over the singing at the end.

title: String Quartet in D minor “Death and the Maiden”
k: string quartet in d minor “death and the maiden” franz schubert · d. 810 · 1824 two violins, viola and cello the g minor slow movement varies the chordal introduction of der tod und das madchen. a sharply accented scherzo and a tarantella finale keep the surrounding movements in motion; all four movements begin in minor keys.

title: Symphony in C major “Great”
k: symphony in c major “great” franz schubert · d. 944 · 1825–26 orchestra, including three trombones a broad horn introduction leads into an allegro driven by dotted rhythms and triplets. the a minor andante con moto grows from an oboe melody into a sustained orchestral crisis. the manuscript bears the date march 1828, but the main composition is generally assigned to 1825–26.

title: Winterreise
k: winterreise franz schubert · d. 911 · 1827 voice and piano; twenty-four poems by wilhelm muller composed in two instalments, in february and october. a steady walking pulse opens gute nacht; by der leiermann, the final song, accompaniment has contracted to the hurdy-gurdy’s bare fifth and small revolving figures. the cycle ends with a question addressed to its player.

title: Two sets of Impromptus
k: two sets of impromptus franz schubert · d. 899 · d. 935 · 1827 piano; four pieces in each set d. 899 no. 3 sustains a g♭ major melody above continuous broken chords; d. 935 no. 3 is a b♭ major variation set on a theme also heard in rosamunde and the a minor quartet. only the first two of d. 899 appeared in schubert’s lifetime.

title: Schwanengesang
k: schwanengesang franz schubert · d. 957 · d. 965a · 1828 voice and piano; poems by ludwig rellstab, heinrich heine and johann gabriel seidl haslinger’s posthumous collection. the heine group includes der doppelganger, whose spare repeated chordal pattern supports the recognition of a figure outside a former lover’s house. die taubenpost, d. 965a, was appended to the thirteen songs catalogued as d. 957.

title: String Quintet in C major
k: string quintet in c major franz schubert · d. 956 · 1828 two violins, viola and two cellos the e major adagio sets a broad inner-voice melody against first-violin interjections and a pizzicato bass, then breaks into f minor. the scherzo’s c major gives way to a d♭ major trio. semitone shifts disturb the large tonal blocks as decisively as the added cello changes the ensemble’s balance.

title: Piano Sonata in B♭ major
k: piano sonata in b♭ major franz schubert · d. 960 · 1828 piano the last completed sonata. a low g♭ trill interrupts the first movement’s opening paragraph; the second movement moves to c♯ minor. its four movements require distinct kinds of pulse: broad molto moderato, the slow movement’s persistent accompaniment, a lightly articulated scherzo and a finale repeatedly interrupted by a single g.

title: Hector Berlioz
k: hector berlioz 1803–1869 · romanticism he made orchestral colour, the position of a sound in space, and the return of a remembered melody into structural events.

title: Symphonie fantastique
k: symphonie fantastique hector berlioz · op. 14 · 1830 orchestra with harps, bells and expanded percussion five movements linked by the idee fixe; the beloved’s melody survives waltz, pastoral, execution and sabbath.

title: Le Roi Lear
k: le roi lear hector berlioz · op. 4 · 1831 orchestra a shakespeare overture written in italy; the slow introduction and ensuing allegro distinguish the king’s authority from the drama it cannot control.

title: Harold en Italie
k: harold en italie hector berlioz · op. 16 · 1834 solo viola and orchestra a four-movement symphony with an observing soloist.

title: Benvenuto Cellini
k: benvenuto cellini hector berlioz · op. 23 · 1834–38 opera the casting of a statue becomes a theatrical crisis; carnival, private intrigue and collective labour intersect.

title: Grande Messe des morts
k: grande messe des morts hector berlioz · op. 5 · 1837 tenor, chorus, large orchestra and four additional brass groups the requiem places unaccompanied choral writing beside its spatially divided brass summons.

title: Roméo et Juliette
k: romeo et juliette hector berlioz · op. 17 · 1839 solo voices, choruses and orchestra a dramatic symphony whose love scene and queen mab scherzo are orchestral; voices frame and complete the action.

title: Grande Symphonie funèbre et triomphale
k: grande symphonie funebre et triomphale hector berlioz · op. 15 · 1840 wind band; later optional strings and chorus written for a public procession; a solo trombone delivers the central funeral oration.

title: Les Nuits d’été
k: les nuits d’ete hector berlioz · op. 7 · 1841; orchestrated by 1856 voice and piano; later voice and orchestra six gautier settings. le spectre de la rose sustains an apparition through long vocal phrases and carefully separated orchestral colours.

title: La Damnation de Faust
k: la damnation de faust hector berlioz · op. 24 · 1845–46 soloists, chorus and orchestra a dramatic legend after goethe, incorporating the hungarian march and marguerite’s d’amour l’ardente flamme.

title: Te Deum
k: te deum hector berlioz · op. 22 · 1849 tenor, multiple choirs, orchestra and organ the organ’s physical separation from the orchestra is part of the conception; first performed in 1855.

title: L’Enfance du Christ
k: l’enfance du christ hector berlioz · op. 25 · 1850–54 soloists, chorus and orchestra three parts trace herod’s dream, the flight into egypt and the arrival at sais; the ishmaelites’ trio uses two flutes and harp.

title: Les Troyens
k: les troyens hector berlioz ·  · 1856–58 opera in five acts virgil’s troy and carthage: cassandra’s warnings, dido’s state, the hunt and storm, and a love duet interrupted by historical duty.

title: Béatrice et Bénédict
k: beatrice et benedict hector berlioz ·  · 1860–62 comic opera in two acts shakespeare’s sparring lovers in a work with spoken dialogue; hero and ursule’s duet suspends the comedy in a nocturnal scene.

title: Fanny Hensel
k: fanny hensel 1805–1847 · romanticism her berlin musical gatherings supported a body of songs, piano cycles and chamber works whose public publication began only near the end of her life.

title: Easter Sonata in A major
k: easter sonata in a major fanny hensel ·  · 1828 piano a four-movement sonata long misattributed to felix; its contrapuntal writing and religious associations belong to fanny’s early large-scale work.

title: Lobgesang
k: lobgesang fanny hensel ·  · 1831 soloists, chorus and orchestra a cantata associated with the birth of her son, sebastian; felix later used the same name for his symphony-cantata.

title: Overture in C major
k: overture in c major fanny hensel ·  · 1832 orchestra a slow introduction opens into an energetic allegro; evidence of orchestral composition beyond the songs and piano collections.

title: String Quartet in E♭ major
k: string quartet in e♭ major fanny hensel ·  · 1834 two violins, viola and cello four movements beginning with an adagio; the romanze and finale make a different balance from the conventional sonata-first quartet.

title: Das Jahr
k: das jahr fanny hensel ·  · 1841 piano twelve months and a postlude; chorales, transitions and recurring material turn a calendar into a continuous large-scale design.

title: Gartenlieder
k: gartenlieder fanny hensel · op. 3 · 1846 unaccompanied mixed voices six part-songs published in 1847, bringing the cultivation of a private vocal ensemble into print.

title: Vier Lieder für das Pianoforte
k: vier lieder fur das pianoforte fanny hensel · op. 2 · 1846 (published) piano four songs for piano: the title asks the performer to distinguish a singing voice from the instrument’s accompanying activity.

title: Piano Trio in D minor
k: piano trio in d minor fanny hensel · op. 11 · 1847 piano, violin and cello a substantial four-movement work, published in 1850; the third movement is a short lied before the expanded finale.

title: Sechs Lieder
k: sechs lieder fanny hensel · op. 7 · 1847 (published) voice and piano includes the eichendorff setting nachtwanderer; the opus number records publication.

title: Felix Mendelssohn
k: felix mendelssohn 1809–1847 · romanticism a composer-conductor who turned quicksilver string writing, bachian counterpoint and remembered landscapes into tightly organised concert music.

title: Octet in E♭ major
k: octet in e♭ major felix mendelssohn · op. 20 · 1825 four violins, two violas and two cellos eight-part chamber writing with orchestral changes of density; the scherzo returns inside the fugal finale.

title: A Midsummer Night’s Dream
k: a midsummer night’s dream felix mendelssohn · opp. 21 and 61 · 1826; 1842 overture; later incidental music with voices and orchestra the overture predates the incidental music by sixteen years. fairies, lovers and tradesmen have different registers, articulations and rhythmic types.

title: Songs without Words
k: songs without words felix mendelssohn ·  · 1829–45 piano the main body of the published collections: melody and accompaniment remain distinct even when shared between the hands.

title: The Hebrides
k: the hebrides felix mendelssohn · op. 26 · 1830–32 orchestra a b minor concert overture grown from an 1829 scottish sketch; also known as fingal’s cave.

title: Symphony No. 4 in A major “Italian”
k: symphony no. 4 in a major “italian” felix mendelssohn · op. 90 · 1833; later revisions orchestra the saltarello finale stays in a minor. the composer’s dissatisfaction kept the work unpublished during his life.

title: St Paul
k: st paul felix mendelssohn · op. 36 · 1836 soloists, chorus and orchestra an oratorio that places chorales and contrapuntal choruses inside a continuous account of conversion and preaching.

title: Piano Trio No. 1 in D minor
k: piano trio no. 1 in d minor felix mendelssohn · op. 49 · 1839 piano, violin and cello the cello’s opening melody spans the piano’s continuous motion; the scherzo demands a different, sharply articulated kind of coordination.

title: Symphony No. 3 in A minor “Scottish”
k: symphony no. 3 in a minor “scottish” felix mendelssohn · op. 56 · 1842 orchestra four connected movements and a concluding a major transformation; the scottish sketches began in 1829.

title: Violin Concerto in E minor
k: violin concerto in e minor felix mendelssohn · op. 64 · 1844 violin and orchestra premiered by ferdinand david in 1845. the soloist enters almost immediately, and the cadenza prepares the recapitulation.

title: Elijah
k: elijah felix mendelssohn · op. 70 · 1846 soloists, chorus and orchestra written for birmingham’s festival; the chorus changes between a desperate population, worshippers of baal and reflective narrator.

title: Frédéric Chopin
k: frederic chopin 1810–1849 · romanticism he made the piano sing through ornament, contrapuntal voice-leading and the unstable accents of polish dance.

title: Variations on “Là ci darem la mano”
k: variations on “la ci darem la mano” frederic chopin · op. 2 · 1827 piano and orchestra mozart’s duet becomes a sequence of contrasting piano textures; the work prompted schumann’s early public advocacy.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in F minor
k: piano concerto no. 2 in f minor frederic chopin · op. 21 · 1829–30 piano and orchestra composed before no. 1. its larghetto makes operatic ornament the centre of the solo part.

title: Twelve Études
k: twelve etudes frederic chopin · op. 10 · 1829–32 piano each technical problem produces a distinctive texture; no. 2 combines a right-hand chromatic scale with accompanying notes in the same hand.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in E minor
k: piano concerto no. 1 in e minor frederic chopin · op. 11 · 1830 piano and orchestra a broad first movement, an e major romance and a finale whose syncopations draw on the krakowiak.

title: Ballade No. 1 in G minor
k: ballade no. 1 in g minor frederic chopin · op. 23 · 1831–35 piano a large single movement whose transformed thematic returns prepare a fast coda.

title: Twelve Études
k: twelve etudes frederic chopin · op. 25 · 1832–37 piano includes studies in thirds, sixths, octaves and contrary motion; the technical task always has a harmonic and melodic function.

title: Two Nocturnes
k: two nocturnes frederic chopin · op. 27 · 1835 piano c♯ minor and d♭ major share a tonic pitch under different spellings; the second sustains a decorated duet above its rocking accompaniment. published in 1836.

title: Twenty-four Preludes
k: twenty-four preludes frederic chopin · op. 28 · 1836–39 piano major and relative-minor pairs move around the circle of fifths, allowing extreme contrasts of scale, register and duration.

title: Piano Sonata No. 2 in B♭ minor
k: piano sonata no. 2 in b♭ minor frederic chopin · op. 35 · 1837–39 piano the funeral march predates the complete sonata; the finale’s unison writing removes the usual distinction between melody and harmony.

title: Ballade No. 4 in F minor
k: ballade no. 4 in f minor frederic chopin · op. 52 · 1842 piano variation and counterpoint gradually intensify the main theme; quiet chords make a break before the coda.

title: Polonaise in A♭ major
k: polonaise in a♭ major frederic chopin · op. 53 · 1842 piano a recurrent polonaise rhythm frames a central passage driven by repeated left-hand octaves.

title: Piano Sonata No. 3 in B minor
k: piano sonata no. 3 in b minor frederic chopin · op. 58 · 1844 piano a four-movement design with a b major largo and a finale whose recurring theme gathers increasing momentum.

title: Barcarolle in F♯ major
k: barcarolle in f♯ major frederic chopin · op. 60 · 1845–46 piano compound metre and a rocking bass support two intertwined singing parts; returns are recomposed through ornament and register.

title: Polonaise-Fantaisie in A♭ major
k: polonaise-fantaisie in a♭ major frederic chopin · op. 61 · 1845–46 piano an introduction of isolated gestures and resonant arpeggios precedes the gradual consolidation of dance and large-scale form.

title: Cello Sonata in G minor
k: cello sonata in g minor frederic chopin · op. 65 · 1845–46 cello and piano written for auguste franchomme; its dense first movement and compact largo reveal two different kinds of instrumental partnership.

title: Robert Schumann
k: robert schumann 1810–1856 · romanticism his music lets remembered fragments, concealed names and competing inner voices interrupt the forms that contain them.

title: Papillons
k: papillons robert schumann · op. 2 · 1829–31 piano a sequence of dances associated with jean paul’s flegeljahre; the close recalls the opening dance as the ball disperses.

title: Carnaval
k: carnaval robert schumann · op. 9 · 1834–35 piano masks and portraits generated from the asch pitch ciphers; the final march remains in triple metre.

title: Symphonic Études
k: symphonic etudes robert schumann · op. 13 · 1834–35; revised later piano a variation design that changes register, density and articulation as if redistributing a theme among orchestral groups.

title: Fantasie in C major
k: fantasie in c major robert schumann · op. 17 · 1836–38 piano three movements; the first’s beethoven quotation and the last’s extended slow span complicate a simple virtuoso-sonata model.

title: Davidsbündlertänze
k: davidsbundlertanze robert schumann · op. 6 · 1837 piano eighteen pieces associated with florestan and eusebius; a motive from clara’s music opens the cycle.

title: Kreisleriana
k: kreisleriana robert schumann · op. 16 · 1838 piano eight movements named for hoffmann’s fictional musician, with abrupt changes of speed, register and harmonic stability.

title: Liederkreis
k: liederkreis robert schumann · op. 39 · 1840 voice and piano; poems by eichendorff twelve songs including mondnacht, waldesgesprach and zwielicht; landscape repeatedly changes into an uncertain speaking presence.

title: Dichterliebe
k: dichterliebe robert schumann · op. 48 · 1840 voice and piano; poems by heine sixteen songs in the published cycle; the piano’s final recollection outlasts the singer’s proposed burial of love and song.

title: Symphony No. 1 in B♭ major “Spring”
k: symphony no. 1 in b♭ major “spring” robert schumann · op. 38 · 1841 orchestra an opening brass call supplies material for a four-movement symphonic design.

title: Symphony No. 4 in D minor
k: symphony no. 4 in d minor robert schumann · op. 120 · 1841; revised 1851 orchestra connected movements and recurring material; the two versions differ in orchestration and details of formal continuity.

title: Piano Quintet in E♭ major
k: piano quintet in e♭ major robert schumann · op. 44 · 1842 piano and string quartet a march-like slow movement and a finale that combines themes from different movements in counterpoint.

title: Piano Concerto in A minor
sub: Robert Schumann · Op. 54 · 1845; from an 1841 Fantasy
k: piano concerto in a minor robert schumann · op. 54 · 1845; from an 1841 fantasy piano and orchestra expanded from an earlier fantasy; the opening theme moves between piano and woodwind.

title: Symphony No. 2 in C major
k: symphony no. 2 in c major robert schumann · op. 61 · 1845–46 orchestra a brass motto frames an argument in which the adagio’s singing line and imitative writing are central.

title: Cello Concerto in A minor
k: cello concerto in a minor robert schumann · op. 129 · 1850 cello and orchestra three connected movements; the soloist’s continuity matters more than a conventional succession of orchestral contests.

title: Symphony No. 3 in E♭ major “Rhenish”
k: symphony no. 3 in e♭ major “rhenish” robert schumann · op. 97 · 1850 orchestra five movements, including a solemn fourth whose compact contrapuntal writing interrupts the surrounding public energy.

title: Violin Concerto in D minor
k: violin concerto in d minor robert schumann ·  · 1853 violin and orchestra written for joachim and withheld after schumann’s death; the finale’s polonaise-like tread differs from a conventional fleet concerto conclusion.

title: Franz Liszt
k: franz liszt 1811–1886 · romanticism the touring pianist who made a single theme change character, and eventually stripped virtuosity down to a few unresolved notes.

title: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 in C♯ minor
k: hungarian rhapsody no. 2 in c♯ minor franz liszt · s. 244/2 · 1851 piano published in 1851. a slow lassu gives way to the accelerating dance-world of the friss; accent, register and flexible tempo imitate the delivery of a band.

title: Transcendental Études
k: transcendental etudes franz liszt · s. 139 · 1852 piano the final form of twelve studies whose first version dates from 1826. mazeppa makes a repeated-note figure drive a large narrative; chasse-neige builds its texture from tremolo.

title: Piano Sonata in B minor
k: piano sonata in b minor franz liszt · s. 178 · 1853 piano one continuous movement in which a few motifs become march, song, slow meditation and fugato. the quiet b major ending replaces an earlier loud conclusion preserved in the manuscript.

title: Les Préludes
k: les preludes franz liszt · s. 97 · 1854 orchestra premiered in weimar in 1854. earlier choral-overture material became a symphonic poem carrying a programme after lamartine; hear how the same thematic family serves lyrical and martial episodes.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in E♭ major
k: piano concerto no. 1 in e♭ major franz liszt · s. 124 · 1855 piano and orchestra premiered in weimar with liszt as soloist and berlioz conducting. its connected sections recall earlier themes in altered functions; the scherzo gives the triangle an unusually exposed role.

title: Années de pèlerinage: Première année, Suisse
k: annees de pelerinage: premiere annee, suisse franz liszt · s. 160 · 1855 piano published in 1855, reworking music from the swiss years. vallee d’obermann turns a questioning descending phrase into an extended argument; au lac de wallenstadt suspends a song above rippling accompaniment.

title: A Faust Symphony
k: a faust symphony franz liszt · s. 108 · 1857 orchestra; tenor and male chorus in the revised ending three character studies: faust, gretchen and mephistopheles. begun in 1854; the choral conclusion was added for 1857. mephistopheles deforms faust’s themes rather than receiving a wholly independent thematic vocabulary.

title: Années de pèlerinage: Deuxième année, Italie
k: annees de pelerinage: deuxieme annee, italie franz liszt · s. 161 · 1858 piano published in 1858. raphael and michelangelo open the book, three petrarch sonnets occupy its centre, and apres une lecture du dante closes it with tritones, tremolos and transformed thematic returns.

title: Les jeux d’eaux à la Villa d’Este
k: les jeux d’eaux a la villa d’este franz liszt · s. 163/4 · 1877 piano part of the third book of annees de pelerinage, published in 1883. its fountains have a scriptural as well as a visual meaning: liszt inserts a latin reference to the water of eternal life from john’s gospel.

title: Nuages gris
k: nuages gris franz liszt · s. 199 · 1881 piano a short late experiment in chromatic bass movement, augmented harmony and an ending that refuses a conventional tonic cadence. much of the argument is carried by bare intervals.

title: Giuseppe Verdi
k: giuseppe verdi 1813–1901 · romanticism an opera composer who made a change of vocal phrase, bass note or ensemble balance alter the relations between people on stage.

title: Nabucco
k: nabucco giuseppe verdi ·  · 1842 opera in four parts; soloists, chorus and orchestra premiered at la scala. the chorus embodies an exiled people; “va, pensiero” is one concentrated point within a score containing much more violent public action.

title: Macbeth
k: macbeth giuseppe verdi ·  · 1847; revised 1865 opera in four acts the florence original and paris revision differ in important numbers and the ending. lady macbeth’s sleepwalking scene requires a controlled, half-withdrawn vocal delivery.

title: Rigoletto
k: rigoletto giuseppe verdi ·  · 1851 opera in three acts premiered at la fenice in venice. the curse, the father–daughter scenes, the quartet and the duke’s returning song tie formal numbers to the consequences of the plot.

title: Il trovatore
k: il trovatore giuseppe verdi ·  · 1853 opera in four parts premiered in rome in january. azucena’s memory of her mother’s execution drives the action; the contrast between sharply defined lyrical forms and extreme violence is deliberate.

title: La traviata
k: la traviata giuseppe verdi ·  · 1853 opera in three acts premiered in venice in march. a contemporary french play becomes a conflict between love, money, respectability and illness; the father–daughter-like negotiation with germont occupies the dramatic centre.

title: Don Carlos
k: don carlos giuseppe verdi ·  · 1867 french opera in five acts; later revised in italian written for paris. the relationship between philip ii and the grand inquisitor places two bass voices against each other; later cuts and revisions substantially alter the work’s historical and personal perspectives.

title: Aida
k: aida giuseppe verdi ·  · 1871 opera in four acts, including stage bands first performed in cairo. public spectacle is counterweighted by sparse scoring at the nile and by the divided stage of the final scene: the entombed lovers below, amneris above.

title: Messa da Requiem
k: messa da requiem giuseppe verdi ·  · 1874 soprano, mezzo-soprano, tenor, bass, chorus and orchestra written in memory of manzoni. offstage trumpets enlarge the tuba mirum; the unaccompanied opening of the agnus dei and the final soprano plea require an entirely different kind of projection.

title: Otello
k: otello giuseppe verdi ·  · 1887 opera in four acts; libretto by arrigo boito first performed at la scala. a storm opens the action without an overture; the long love duet, iago’s credo and desdemona’s willow song inhabit different dramatic and vocal forms.

title: Falstaff
k: falstaff giuseppe verdi ·  · 1893 opera in three acts; libretto by arrigo boito first performed at la scala. small melodic gestures pass rapidly between voices and instruments, interrupted by sustained lyric moments for nannetta and fenton. the final ensemble is a fugue.

title: Richard Wagner
k: richard wagner 1813–1883 · romanticism an opera composer who made the orchestra remember what the characters conceal, and built a theatre for the result.

title: Der fliegende Holländer
k: der fliegende hollander richard wagner · wwv 63 · 1841 opera in three acts; soloists, chorus and orchestra premiered in dresden in 1843. storm music, senta’s ballad and the contrast between living and ghostly sailors bind the legend to recurring musical material; the ending was subsequently revised.

title: Tannhäuser
k: tannhauser richard wagner · wwv 70 · 1845 opera in three acts the dresden original and the revisions associated with paris in 1861 differ substantially, especially in the venusberg music. pilgrimage, sensuality and formal song competition occupy audibly different musical spaces.

title: Lohengrin
k: lohengrin richard wagner · wwv 75 · 1848 opera in three acts premiered by liszt in weimar in 1850. the prelude begins in a divided, high violin register; public ceremony and private mistrust eventually destroy the marriage at the centre of the plot.

title: Das Rheingold
k: das rheingold richard wagner · wwv 86a · 1854 music drama in one continuous evening; large orchestra the preliminary evening of the ring. first staged separately in munich in 1869, against wagner’s preference for a complete cycle. the opening e♭ field accumulates motion before introducing harmonic change.

title: Die Walküre
k: die walkure richard wagner · wwv 86b · 1856 music drama in three acts premiered separately in munich in 1870. the first act builds from a storm and a stranger’s arrival to the recognition of siegmund and sieglinde; wotan’s farewell in act iii makes remembered motifs carry the cost of his decision.

title: Wesendonck-Lieder
k: wesendonck-lieder richard wagner · wwv 91 · 1857–58 voice and piano five settings of mathilde wesendonck. im treibhaus and traume are designated studies for tristan. the familiar orchestral cycle largely uses felix mottl’s later scoring; wagner himself orchestrated traume.

title: Tristan und Isolde
k: tristan und isolde richard wagner · wwv 90 · 1859 opera in three acts first performed in munich in 1865. the prelude’s chromatic voice-leading becomes the opera’s method of postponement; the cor anglais shepherd’s tune in act iii provides an exposed contrast to the crowded orchestral memories.

title: Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg
k: die meistersinger von nurnberg richard wagner · wwv 96 · 1867 opera in three acts; soloists, chorus and orchestra premiered in munich in 1868. song, counterpoint and spoken inflection are made into subjects of the plot. sachs’s reflections on delusion coexist with the exclusionary nationalism of his final address.

title: Siegfried Idyll
k: siegfried idyll richard wagner · wwv 103 · 1870 small orchestra first played privately at tribschen on christmas morning. music shared with siegfried is recast in chamber proportions; the later published version permits larger string forces.

title: Siegfried
k: siegfried richard wagner · wwv 86c · 1871 music drama in three acts its composition was interrupted for twelve years between acts ii and iii. forging, forest listening and the awakening of brunnhilde require different kinds of orchestral motion; the completed work was premiered at bayreuth in 1876.

title: Götterdämmerung
k: gotterdammerung richard wagner · wwv 86d · 1874 prologue and three acts; soloists, chorus and large orchestra the cycle’s conclusion, first heard in 1876. the funeral march recalls a biography through motifs; the final orchestral pages juxtapose memories whose dramatic owners have died or lost their power.

title: Parsifal
k: parsifal richard wagner · wwv 111 · 1882 stage consecration festival play in three acts first performed at bayreuth under hermann levi. ceremonial repetition, compressed chromatic episodes and the transformation music give the three acts different experiences of time.

title: Clara Schumann
k: clara schumann 1819–1896 · romanticism a concert pianist for more than sixty years, she composed songs, chamber music and piano works whose technical demands arise from the independence of their voices.

title: Romance variée in C major
k: romance variee in c major clara schumann · op. 3 · 1831–33 piano dedicated to robert schumann; its melody became material for his op. 5 impromptus.

title: Piano Concerto in A minor
k: piano concerto in a minor clara schumann · op. 7 · 1833–35 piano and orchestra three connected movements. the central romance becomes a piano–cello duet; clara premiered the complete concerto under mendelssohn in 1835.

title: Three Romances
k: three romances clara schumann · op. 11 · 1838–39 piano a set in e♭ major, g minor and a♭ major; the melodic surface depends on careful separation of moving inner parts.

title: Three songs from Rückert’s Liebesfrühling
k: three songs from ruckert’s liebesfruhling clara schumann · op. 12 · 1841 voice and piano published within the joint collection with robert’s op. 37; includes liebst du um schonheit.

title: Scherzo No. 2 in C minor
k: scherzo no. 2 in c minor clara schumann · op. 14 · 1841 piano a concert work whose forceful articulation and registral contrasts differ sharply from the romances.

title: Piano Trio in G minor
k: piano trio in g minor clara schumann · op. 17 · 1846 piano, violin and cello four movements; the finale integrates contrapuntal entries into a sustained sonata argument.

title: Variations on a Theme by Robert Schumann
k: variations on a theme by robert schumann clara schumann · op. 20 · 1853 piano seven variations on bunte blatter, op. 99 no. 4, in f♯ minor; brahms later used the same theme for his op. 9.

title: Three Romances
k: three romances clara schumann · op. 21 · 1853 piano the opening a minor movement and the contrasting f major and g minor pieces explore different kinds of sustained keyboard line.

title: Three Romances
k: three romances clara schumann · op. 22 · 1853 violin and piano dedicated to joseph joachim; the piano carries active harmonic and contrapuntal material alongside the violin’s melody.

title: Anton Bruckner
k: anton bruckner 1824–1896 · romanticism a church organist who built symphonic movements from long harmonic spans, separate instrumental blocks and the silences between them.

title: Mass No. 2 in E minor
k: mass no. 2 in e minor anton bruckner · wab 27 · 1866 eight-part mixed chorus and fifteen wind instruments composed for celebrations associated with linz’s new cathedral and first performed in 1869; later revised. choral counterpoint is supported by winds without strings, making the independence of the vocal parts particularly audible.

title: Mass No. 3 in F minor
k: mass no. 3 in f minor anton bruckner · wab 28 · 1868 four soloists, chorus, orchestra and organ first performed in vienna in 1872. large-scale fugues and returning material connect the liturgical sections; the work stands beside the early symphonies in its own right.

title: Symphony No. 3 in D minor
k: symphony no. 3 in d minor anton bruckner · wab 103 · 1873 orchestra dedicated to wagner. the 1873, 1877 and 1889 versions differ substantially; the earliest contains wagner quotations that were largely removed in revision. the exposed opening trumpet idea gives the movement a long-range point of reference.

title: Symphony No. 4 in E♭ major “Romantic”
k: symphony no. 4 in e♭ major “romantic” anton bruckner · wab 104 · 1874 orchestra substantially rewritten in 1878–80 and revised again later. the familiar horn call and “hunting” scherzo belong to the later conception; the first version has a different scherzo and finale.

title: Symphony No. 5 in B♭ major
k: symphony no. 5 in b♭ major anton bruckner · wab 105 · 1876 orchestra revised through 1878. a slow introduction establishes widely separated gestures; the finale recalls earlier movements and combines fugue subjects with a brass chorale in its concluding span.

title: Symphony No. 6 in A major
k: symphony no. 6 in a major anton bruckner · wab 106 · 1881 orchestra the first movement pits an insistent string rhythm against a broad low-string theme. the adagio’s oboe line and funeral-march material offer contrasting kinds of sustained motion.

title: Symphony No. 7 in E major
k: symphony no. 7 in e major anton bruckner · wab 107 · 1883 orchestra including four wagner tubas premiered in leipzig in 1884. the long opening melody grows over tremolo; the c♯ minor adagio places the wagner tubas within a carefully paced sequence of returns and climaxes.

title: Te Deum in C major
k: te deum in c major anton bruckner · wab 45 · 1884 four soloists, chorus, orchestra and organ a concentrated large choral work. octaves and open fifths give the opening a public, declarative profile; the final fugue sets “in te, domine, speravi”.

title: Symphony No. 8 in C minor
k: symphony no. 8 in c minor anton bruckner · wab 108 · 1887; revised 1890 large orchestra including wagner tubas and harps the revised version was premiered in vienna in 1892. the slow movement’s harp colour is exceptional within bruckner’s symphonies; the finale gathers material from all four movements into its closing c major.

title: Symphony No. 9 in D minor (unfinished)
k: symphony no. 9 in d minor (unfinished) anton bruckner · wab 109 · 1887–96 orchestra including wagner tubas three movements completed by 1894, with extensive material for a fourth. the violent scherzo and the adagio’s dissonant climax belong to a work conceived with a further finale.

title: Johannes Brahms
k: johannes brahms 1833–1897 · romanticism a composer who made a small interval generate a large form, and let conflicting rhythms keep a familiar melody unsettled.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in D minor
k: piano concerto no. 1 in d minor johannes brahms · op. 15 · 1859 piano and orchestra premiered in hanover in 1859 after years of revision. the long orchestral opening and the soloist’s subdued first entry reject the usual division between introductory tutti and virtuoso display.

title: Variations and Fugue on a Theme by Handel
k: variations and fugue on a theme by handel johannes brahms · op. 24 · 1861 piano twenty-five variations and a fugue on an aria from handel’s b♭ keyboard suite, hwv 434. listen to the bass and phrase lengths: they provide continuity when the surface rhythm changes completely.

title: Piano Quintet in F minor
k: piano quintet in f minor johannes brahms · op. 34 · 1864 piano, two violins, viola and cello the final instrumentation followed versions for string quintet and two pianos. its opening unison exposes material that later thickens into contrapuntal exchanges between keyboard and strings.

title: Ein deutsches Requiem
k: ein deutsches requiem johannes brahms · op. 45 · 1865–68 soprano, baritone, chorus and orchestra german biblical texts selected by brahms. the seven movements frame the living mourners and the blessed dead with related words and musical proportions.

title: Variations on a Theme by Joseph Haydn
k: variations on a theme by joseph haydn johannes brahms · op. 56a · 1873 orchestra; also a two-piano version, op. 56b the “st anthony chorale” theme came from a wind work then attributed to haydn; that attribution is not secure. its five-bar phrases remain identifiable beneath the variations and the finale’s repeated bass pattern.

title: Symphony No. 1 in C minor
k: symphony no. 1 in c minor johannes brahms · op. 68 · 1876 orchestra the finale proceeds through a dark introduction, a horn call and a brass chorale before its c major allegro. the opening movement’s opposed chromatic lines give the later release a specific harmonic history.

title: Symphony No. 2 in D major
k: symphony no. 2 in d major johannes brahms · op. 73 · 1877 orchestra a three-note bass cell quietly starts a work whose lyricism repeatedly encounters low-brass interruptions and minor-mode shadows. the finale’s restraint makes its eventual loud conclusion a change of behaviour.

title: Violin Concerto in D major
k: violin concerto in d major johannes brahms · op. 77 · 1878 violin and orchestra written for joachim, who gave the premiere in leipzig on new year’s day 1879. the slow movement begins with an extended oboe melody before the violin offers its own elaboration.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in B♭ major
k: piano concerto no. 2 in b♭ major johannes brahms · op. 83 · 1881 piano and orchestra four movements, including a d minor scherzo. the opening horn call receives a solo-piano answer; the slow movement gives a cello a role closer to chamber partner than orchestral accompaniment.

title: Symphony No. 3 in F major
k: symphony no. 3 in f major johannes brahms · op. 90 · 1883 orchestra f major and f minor contend from the opening f–a♭–f gesture. every movement ends quietly; the finale eventually brings back the first movement’s opening material without a triumphal coda.

title: Symphony No. 4 in E minor
k: symphony no. 4 in e minor johannes brahms · op. 98 · 1884–85 orchestra the first movement grows from a chain of thirds; the last builds variations over an eight-bar progression. trombones, held back until the finale, change the weight of the orchestral argument.

title: Clarinet Quintet in B minor
k: clarinet quintet in b minor johannes brahms · op. 115 · 1891 clarinet, two violins, viola and cello written for richard muhlfeld. the clarinet blends into the strings as often as it rises above them; the finale’s variations lead to a recollection of the opening movement.

title: Modest Mussorgsky
k: modest mussorgsky 1839–1881 · romanticism he made russian speech, public crowds and the noises of ordinary life determine the shape of opera.

title: Salammbô
k: salammbo modest mussorgsky ·  · 1863–66 opera after flaubert an abandoned historical opera whose music was partly absorbed into later projects, including boris godunov.

title: Kalistrat
k: kalistrat modest mussorgsky ·  · 1864 voice and piano; poem by nikolai nekrasov a mother’s prediction of wealth is heard against the adult son’s poverty. the discrepancy between remembered song and present speech supplies the drama.

title: St John’s Night on the Bare Mountain
k: st john’s night on the bare mountain modest mussorgsky ·  · 1867 orchestra the original witches’ sabbath; the familiar rimsky-korsakov arrangement dates from 1886. mussorgsky’s version remained unperformed in his lifetime.

title: The Marriage
k: the marriage modest mussorgsky ·  · 1868 opera after gogol; one act in vocal score an experiment in setting prose dialogue without converting it into regular operatic verse.

title: The Nursery
k: the nursery modest mussorgsky ·  · 1868–72 voice and piano; seven songs to mussorgsky’s own texts children speak, complain, pray and play; the changes of tempo and metre are part of the characterisation.

title: Boris Godunov
k: boris godunov modest mussorgsky ·  · 1868–72 opera after pushkin; soloists, chorus and orchestra authorial versions of 1869 and 1872; first staged in 1874. the tsar’s monologues and the people’s public rituals require different kinds of musical time.

title: Khovanshchina
k: khovanshchina modest mussorgsky ·  · 1872–80 historical opera; soloists, chorus and orchestra religious and political factions confront the coming petrine state. any performance necessarily includes editorial decisions about scoring and completion.

title: Sunless
k: sunless modest mussorgsky ·  · 1874 voice and piano; six poems by arseny golenishchev-kutuzov private rooms, remembered meetings and interrupted thought; the piano often supplies very little, making each harmonic change conspicuous.

title: Pictures at an Exhibition
k: pictures at an exhibition modest mussorgsky ·  · 1874 piano ten pictures linked and penetrated by versions of the promenade. dedicated to vladimir stasov and prompted by the hartmann memorial exhibition.

title: The Fair at Sorochyntsi
k: the fair at sorochyntsi modest mussorgsky ·  · 1874–80 comic opera after gogol village courtship and supernatural interference; the dream scene incorporates material associated with night on bald mountain.

title: Songs and Dances of Death
k: songs and dances of death modest mussorgsky ·  · 1875–77 voice and piano; four poems by golenishchev-kutuzov “lullaby”, “serenade”, “trepak” and “the field marshal”: death appropriates four familiar kinds of song.

title: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
k: pyotr ilyich tchaikovsky 1840–1893 · romanticism he used the timing of dance and theatre to make a symphony’s return, interruption or collapse physically audible.

title: Symphony No. 1 in G minor “Winter Daydreams”
